subject: Request: Full (redacted) penetration test report + remediation timeline
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@horizonclinic.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@horizonclinic.com>, Horizon Clinic Security <security@horizonclinic.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:32:00 -0400
Subject: Request: full penetration test report and remediation details (urgent)

Hi Hannah,

Following public reports of a supply-chain security issue affecting a third-party analytics vendor, our risk and procurement teams are pausing new integrations pending evidence that critical vendors have completed recent security assessments and remediation. We use Redwood for inference in a patient-data-adjacent workflow, and we need the following to clear the procurement hold: 

- A redacted copy of your most recent external penetration test report (redactions for IPs, internal hostnames, and screenshots are fine).
- A remediation status matrix listing each finding, severity, date discovered, fix applied, and whether a retest was completed.
- Confirmation of whether any issues were classified as critical/high and whether those were exploited in any production incidents.

Can you provide the redacted report and remediation matrix? If you have a secure portal or SSO link to share, that works as well. We need this by EOD Wednesday (2026-07-14) to keep our integration timeline.

If necessary, please escalate internally — our security lead is copied.

Thanks,
Alex Morgan
Senior Security Engineer
Horizon Clinic
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@horizonclinic.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 16:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: full penetration test report and remediation details (urgent)

Hi Alex — thanks for the note and the heads up. I understand the procurement urgency and have looped in Marcus (security) and Lauren (CS lead) to coordinate. Quick responses to your asks: 

- We can share a redacted external penetration test report via our secure share link. It will redact IPs, internal hostnames, and attachment screenshots by default.
- We can provide a remediation matrix; Marcus will attach an export showing status per finding.
- No open production incidents related to findings in the last external assessment. Any findings classified as high/critical were remediated and retested.

I'm marking this as high priority and will escalate if we need legal signoff on redactions. Expect an initial packet from Marcus by tomorrow morning (Mon 7/13). If you prefer a short sync to walk through the report, Lauren can set up a 30-minute call.

Best,
Hannah
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@horizonclinic.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: full penetration test report and remediation details (urgent)

Hi Alex — Marcus from Product Security here. Attaching a redacted export of our external pentest (attached as horizonclinic_pt_redacted_v1.pdf) and a remediation matrix (horizon_remediation_matrix_20260713.csv). Summary below: 

Executive summary:
- External assessment performed 2026-05-18 through 2026-05-22 by third-party vendor VeritasSec.
- Total findings: 12 (0 critical, 3 high, 5 medium, 4 low).
- High findings addressed between 2026-05-25 and 2026-06-10; retests completed 2026-06-15.
- No evidence of production exploitation related to these findings. Audit logs and endpoint telemetry were reviewed during remediation; no anomalous access tied to the findings was observed.

Notable items (linked to remediation matrix):
- High: insecure default config in a non-production model training cluster — hardened and credentials rotated; verification via retest.
- High: outdated third-party dependency in a build system — upgraded and CI gating added; retest validated.
- High: two SSRF variants in an internal admin endpoint — endpoint removed from internet-facing surface and WAF rule applied; retest validated.

We redact hostnames, internal IPs, and PoC screenshots in the attached PDF. If Horizon requires unredacted artifacts under an NDA or an in-person review, we can discuss an escalation path with Legal.

I also created a short remediation CSV with status, owner, first reported, date fixed, and retest date. That file is attached. If you need additional evidence (change control tickets, CVE patch commits, or post-fix logs), specify which items you'd like and we'll pull them.

Attachments:
- horizonclinic_pt_redacted_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.3MB)
- horizon_remediation_matrix_20260713.csv (CSV, 24KB)

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@horizonclinic.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@horizonclinic.com>, Horizon Clinic Security <security@horizonclinic.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 12:48:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: full penetration test report and remediation details (urgent)

Marcus — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few follow-ups from our risk team after a preliminary review: 

1) The procurement team asked for explicit proof of retests for the three high findings (change IDs or ticket links and the retest verification logs). The remediation CSV has dates, but we need traceable artifacts.
2) For the SSRF fixes, we need to understand exposure windows — can you provide the earliest reported date and confirmation there were no associated anomalous requests in that window?
3) We are prepared to sign an NDA for an unredacted copy if Redwood requires it; please advise next steps and an estimated turnaround for unredacted evidence.

This is blocking our integration kickoff; we need the extra proof by EOD Wednesday (2026-07-14) to avoid further delay. If you can't make that deadline, please advise a date and whether Legal will need to be involved.

If it's easier, we can take the evidence in a secured S3 bucket with pre-signed links and a short-lived access token.

Thanks,
Alex
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@horizonclinic.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 13:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: full penetration test report and remediation details (urgent)

Alex — quick update and next steps: 

- Marcus and Rishi will pull the retest verification artifacts and change-control ticket IDs today. We will provide those as secured, time-limited links (S3 pre-signed) to Horizon Security by EOD Wednesday 2026-07-14.
- For SSRF exposure windows, Marcus will include the first-reported timestamp and a short review of request logs; we will explicitly call out the observation window in the evidence bundle.
- We are amenable to an NDA for full unredacted materials. If you send a copy of your standard vendor security NDA, Legal will review; otherwise we can propose Redwood's standard mutual NDA (I can share a link).

I appreciate the urgency — we will escalate internally if anything slips. Lauren will reach out to schedule a 30-minute walkthrough for Thursday if that helps accelerate approvals.

Best,
Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192
